Why go: Pig Island and Koh Tan by speedboat

Pig Island is the nickname of Koh Madsum, a small island off the south-west coast of Koh Samui where a family of pigs lives on a white-sand beach and wanders into the shallows. Boats leave from Thong Krut, a fishing village on Samui's south-west tip, and the speedboat crossing takes 15–30 minutes. Next door is Koh Tan, with a shallow reef close to the beach that is the better snorkelling stop of the two. Masks and snorkels are provided, and kayaks are on board when the sea allows. The captain sets the order of the stops to suit the tide, and the trip ends with a Thai meal on the beach.

This is the shortest and best-value Pig Island trip: 4–5 hours door to door for 1,450 THB, with your hotel transfer, guide, snorkel gear, soft drinks and the meal included. Two departures make it easy to fit into a week. The morning trip (pickup around 08:30, back around 14:15) includes lunch and usually has the calmest sea. The afternoon trip (pickup around 13:00, back around 18:30) includes dinner and catches softer light on the beach.

Be clear about what it is: a short, easy island hop in sheltered water, not a full-day wilderness park like Ang Thong. That is also its strength. Koh Madsum and Koh Tan are not in a national park, so this trip runs every day of the year, weather permitting, including 1 November–15 December when Ang Thong is closed. Compared with our other Pig Island options, the speedboat is fastest and cheapest. The longtail is slower and more traditional with no more than 12 guests, and the sunset tour adds the evening light.

Meeting the pigs responsibly

  • Watch, photograph and let the pigs come to you. Don't chase, lift or ride them, and leave the piglets alone.
  • Feed only what island staff provide, if anything. Never bring crisps, bread or sweets.
  • Give them space in the midday heat, when they rest in the shade.
  • Wash your hands after contact, and keep food bags closed on the beach.

Who this tour is for

  • Families: the crossing is short, the beach is shallow and children's life jackets are provided. Children aged 3–11 pay the child price and infants up to 2 travel free.
  • First-timers who want the pigs, a snorkel and a meal without giving up a whole day.
  • Visitors in November and early December, when Ang Thong is closed.
  • Non-swimmers: snorkelling is optional, and you can float in a life jacket or stay on the beach.

Who should choose another tour

  • Want a slower, quieter day with lunch on Koh Tan: the small-group longtail.
  • Want sunset over the sea: the Pig Island sunset tour with dinner.
  • Hoping to see dolphins: the Pink Dolphins and Pig Island tour.
  • Your own group and timing: the private longtail (5,950 THB per boat) or the private speedboat (11,950 THB per boat).
  • Pregnant or with back or neck problems: speedboats bounce on choppy water. Choose the longtail, and check with your doctor.
  • Want limestone cliffs and viewpoints: the Ang Thong speedboat tour (from 16 December).

What to bring

  • Cash in small notes for the Koh Madsum island fee (about 50 THB per person) and for drinks or snacks on the islands.
  • Swimwear, a towel and a change of clothes.
  • Reef-safe sunscreen, a hat and sunglasses.
  • Water shoes or sandals: the shallows have rocks and coral rubble in places.
  • A waterproof phone pouch or dry bag.
  • Fins, if you want them (not provided).
  • Your booking confirmation on your phone.

Good to know

  • Sea by month: the water between Thong Krut and the islands is short and fairly sheltered. January to September is best; February to April is calmest. October to December is the rainy season, with showers most days; trips still run when the sea is safe. Strong wind can cancel any boat, and if we cancel you choose a full refund or a new date.
  • Tides: the tide affects beach landings and how much sand there is for the pigs. The captain adjusts the order of stops; see our tide times.
  • Seasickness: if you are prone to it, take the morning departure, which usually has the calmer sea.
  • Snorkelling: visibility at Koh Tan is best from February to September and drops after heavy rain. Don't stand on the coral.
  • Mobility: boarding is from a pier or the beach, sometimes in knee-deep water. There are no climbs on the standard route.
  • Children: children's life jackets are provided and children wear them at all times on the boat.
  • Photography and drones: the pigs are easy to photograph from a metre or two away. If you fly a drone (registered with the CAAT and NBTC), ask the captain first and never fly low over the animals or other visitors.
  • Rubbish: take every wrapper and bottle back to the boat.

Pickup and meeting point

Minibus transfers to Thong Krut pier are included from the main areas of Koh Samui: Chaweng, Lamai, Bophut, Maenam, Choeng Mon, Bang Rak and Plai Laem. Remote areas cost 400 THB per person return; the booking card shows any surcharge for your area. Thong Krut is about 45–60 minutes by road from Chaweng and 30–40 minutes from Lamai. We send your exact pickup time by 18:00 the day before. If the minibus can't reach your hotel or villa road, we send a nearby meeting point with a map pin. Staying nearby? You can meet the boat at Thong Krut pier; message us on WhatsApp first.
